Maria Huang: Quick sync — Product told me there's a phased Q4 push that overlaps Black Friday. Can we get a worst-case GPU-hour + tail-latency plan and a cost delta? Need numbers and fallback options :rocket:
Kenji Saito: Got it. Rough quick ballpark: 3x sustained spike for ~36h -> O(10k) GPU-hours on p4d equiv. I'll run sim with region splits. Which regions are in-scope?
Sasha Patel: US + EU are primary, APAC small but time-shifted. Prefer prewarm in us-west1 and eu-west4, avoid cross-region hot swap if possible (egress costs).
Ryan Lopez: Current reserved: us-west1=80 GPUs, eu-west4=40 GPUs. Spot pool across both can add ~30% capacity but preemption risk is non-trivial.
ops-bot: capacity-forecast-service: queued simulation for thread 1783007890 (config: q4_bf_overlap).
Kenji Saito: I'll run two sims: A) aggressive reserved + minimal spot (lower risk), B) lean reserved + heavy spot (cost optimized). Will include hourly curves and tail-latency prob.
Maria Huang: Please include est cost delta vs baseline, and the expected p95/p99 tail latencies. Also flag any single-region failure modes.
Kenji Saito: Quick paste from local sim run (preliminary):
```
config A:
- peak_throughput: 220k reqs/hr
- gpu-hours (36h window): 8,100
- est cost delta (36h delta normalized to monthly): $72,000
- p95 latency: 120ms, p99: 420ms

config B:
- peak_throughput: 240k reqs/hr (more batching, higher throughput)
- gpu-hours (36h window): 6,400
- est cost delta: $48,000
- risk: ~20% chance of p99 spikes >1s during spot preemptions
```
Sasha Patel: For config B we need stronger fallbacks: routed model-variants (smaller quantized variant) + canary pool in us-east1 so we don't fully rely on eu/us-west. Also document the model quality regression tolerance.
Ryan Lopez: Networking note: eu-west4 peering IGW currently has ~6 Gbps spare. Embedding-heavy responses could saturate that during peak (we saw similar pattern in last promo). Consider compressing outputs, moving reranking server-side, or temporarily routing EU traffic to eu-central with better peering. Also check inter-region egress cost delta.
Maria Huang: Good catch. Include egress cost in the delta. Also list runbook steps for automatic fallback (which model variant, which region to spill to).
Kenji Saito: I'll run a fine-grained sim with per-region hourly curves and simulate spot preemption patterns. Will also run a cold-start prewarm test for container boot times (~RPS ramp test). Command I'm using locally: `rwd capacity simulate --scenario q4-bf-overlap --regions us-west1,eu-west4,us-east1 --window 36h --spots`
Maria Huang: Nice. Can you also output the simulation as a small CSV so finance can eyeball the $ numbers?
Kenji Saito: Yes — will attach CSV to the thread by EOD PST.
Sasha Patel: I'll draft a short fallback runbook: 1) auto-fallback to quantized-2x model variant 2) spill to us-east1 canary 3) disable heavy embeddings by flag. Will post draft.
Ryan Lopez: I'll run peering throughput test tonight and post any suggested route changes + egress cost estimate. Also check NAT gateway scaling for us-west1.
Maria Huang: Action items summary :small_blue_diamond:
- Kenji: full sims with CSV + tail-latency probabilities + cold-start prewarm test (EOD PST)
- Ryan: peering + egress cost + NAT scaling check (tonight)
- Sasha: fallback runbook + variant pinning plan (tomorrow AM)
I'll sync with Product on marketing cadence after we have numbers.
Kenji Saito: Will update here.
ops-bot: prewarm-service: kicked prewarm job prewarm/us-west1/1783008001 (status: started).
